accuracy_findings.claim: "So no agent can join the board until that lex is active. Buying it is not enough." (paragraph 2, about [[lex/agent]] Age of Exploration)
accuracy_findings.problem: False at every speed. Age of Exploration is only the root of the tree, so you must own it before buying anything else. Its effect is not needed, though. Any active lex that raises an agent limit lets agents join the board, even when Age of Exploration is not active. A player who owns Age of Exploration and Reaction Force and makes only Reaction Force active has a Navarch Limit of 2 and can activate Navarchs. The 'one exception is Open Court' sentence then inherits the same error, because Open Court is not the only other way.
accuracy_findings.evidence: tmp/help-review/agent-limits-acc-r0-probe.exs calls the real Player.update_policies/2 with doctrines [:agent, :admiral_1]. slow: none active {0,0,0}; [:agent] {2,2,2}; only [:admiral_1] {2,0,0}, character_available_slots?(:admiral) = true. The same at medium. fast: [:agent] {1,1,1}; only [:admiral_1] {2,0,0}, slot free = true. With nothing active, slot free = false at all speeds. Code: player.ex:1297-1305 compares only the on-board count to max_admirals, whatever lex supplies it. doctrine-{slow,medium,fast}.ex: :agent is the only ancestor:nil node, and admiral_1, spy_1 and the others descend from it.
accuracy_findings.fix: Say what is true: the limits come only from active lexes, and Age of Exploration is the root of the tree, so you must buy it before any other lex. A bought lex does nothing until it is active. For example: "All three start at 0. Only [[active-lexes|active lexes]] raise them. [[lex/agent]] is the first lex you can buy, and a lex does nothing until it is active, so no agent can join the board until at least one lex that raises its limit is active. votes.reason: The rule is clear (limits start at 0, only active lexes raise them, deck agents don't count), but a few terms and the lex-activation path are left undefined or hard to parse.
stumbles: "The Open Court game modifier also adds 1 to each limit, and it is not in the tables below" - I don't know what Open Court is or whether my game has it, so I can't tell if my limits are 0 or 1.

"buying, on the market, an agent that another player sells straight from their board, because it joins your board at once" - a long, twisty sentence. It's unclear how this differs from a normal market purchase.

The page never says what Navarchs, Erased and Siderians are, or how many lexes can be active at once, so I can't tell whether Age of Exploration plus another lex is possible for me. The tables also show no lex cost or lock time, so I can't tell which source is worth buying next.

votes.reason: The rule, the three limits, and what counts as on the board are clear and the tables are easy to scan, but the summed limit and the Open Court bonus are left for the player to work out.
stumbles: "All three start at 0 ... The Open Court game modifier also adds 1 to each limit, and it is not in the tables below." It says start at 0, then adds a hidden +1, and never states the actual starting value or how to tell whether Open Court is on.

"Every active source adds to it." There is no worked total or maximum, so a skimmer has to add up the table rows themselves. Example: Erased shows +2, +2, +4, +7, +7, +2, +2, and it is unclear whether every lex can be active at once.

"buying, on the market, an agent that another player sells straight from their board, because it joins your board at once" is a dense sentence, and "Hiring an agent puts it in your deck, so the limits never block hiring" leaves it unclear how hiring differs from buying.
